- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; increase forecast gradually, not abruptly.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; anchor forecast to 14-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) and price is trending up.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2–0.4), model often overfits to recent highs; use 30-day average as baseline, then add 0.5–1.5% if sentiment >0.5, else subtract 0.5–1.5%.
